title: Attackers have been exploiting critical Zimbra flaw to steal emails
gist: Microsoft warns that attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-73570, an unauthenticated OS command injection in Zimbra Collaboration Suite reached via SMTP to the SNMP notification path, to deploy web shells and collect email backups and credentials. Shadowserver counted 274 compromised instances. The exposed install base fell from 19,000 to about 10,000 after Synacor's July 20 patch, which Synacor did not disclose for more than three weeks.

insights.claim: Microsoft says attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-73570 in Zimbra Collaboration Suite, which lets them run OS commands remotely without authentication, to obtain organizations' email backups and authentication credentials.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Self-hosted mail servers remain high-value targets, which supports demand for managed email and email security.

insights.claim: The Shadowserver Foundation found 274 compromised Zimbra Collaboration Suite instances, and the number of internet-exposed ZCS servers fell from about 19,000 the week after the patch to about 10,000 now.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: The shrinking install base may reflect organizations migrating off self-hosted Zimbra.

insights.claim: Microsoft observed affected organizations in more than one region and industry, so the exploitation was not limited to one sector or geography. Attribution was not provided.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: This looks like an opportunistic, broad campaign rather than a targeted one.
insights.quote: Based on the environments investigated, exploitation was not limited to a single sector or geographic area.

insights.claim: From July 28 to August 7, two distinct scanning tools probed for vulnerable Zimbra endpoints, first confirming command execution through out-of-band DNS, ICMP and HTTP callbacks before deploying JSP web shells, reverse shells, privilege escalation and persistence tooling.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Attackers validated the exploit at scale before committing payloads, a typical precursor to mass exploitation.

insights.claim: CVE-2026-73570 can only be exploited when the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled. A crafted SMTP request then injects shell commands that run with the zimbra service account's privileges.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Exposure depends on configuration, so the vulnerable population is a subset of all installs.
insights.quote: An attacker can send a specially crafted SMTP request that introduces untrusted input into SNMP notification processing

insights.claim: Zimbra maintainer Synacor patched the flaw on July 20 but did not disclose the vulnerability for more than three weeks, while scanning activity began July 28. Admins should run ZCS 10.1.20 or later.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Slow disclosure left customers exposed and creates reputational risk for Synacor's Zimbra franchise.
